???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What is the difference between a loop-carried and a loop-independent dependence?"

        A loop-independent dependence links accesses in the same iteration and is never affected by reordering iterations. A loop-carried dependence links accesses in different iterations, and only it constrains how a loop may be run.

        Introduced in [P6. Dependence analysis](p6-dependence-analysis.md).

    ??? question "What is the difference between latency and reciprocal throughput?"

        Latency is how long one instruction takes to produce its result; reciprocal throughput is how often independent instructions of that kind can start. A loop-carried chain waits on latency; independent chains hide it.

        Introduced in [P5. The microarchitecture shelf](p5-microarchitecture.md).

    ??? question "What is a cache line?"

        The fixed-size, aligned chunk a cache moves in one transfer; the unit a fetch actually costs, not one value. Two addresses sharing a line move together whether or not the code touching them is related.

        Introduced in [P2. The memory hierarchy](p2-memory-hierarchy.md).
